title: test-0100-SCI-BIO-RESPIRATION
passage: Respiration is a fundamental biological process that occurs in all living cells, not just within lungs or specialized organs. At its core, cellular respiration is the chemical breakdown of glucose to release energy, a process that continues constantly in every living cell, including those in plants and roots, regardless of whether it is day or night. While breathing is the physical act of inhaling and exhaling air to exchange gases, respiration is the internal metabolic process that uses oxygen to produce energy and releases carbon dioxide as a byproduct. When we breathe, we do not inhale pure oxygen or exhale pure carbon dioxide; instead, we take in a mixture of atmospheric gases and release a mixture containing more carbon dioxide than we inhaled. In plants, gas exchange occurs through tiny pores called stomata, which facilitate the movement of oxygen and carbon dioxide for both respiration and photosynthesis. Even in environments like soil or water, organisms must access oxygen to survive. Roots absorb oxygen trapped in soil spaces, and fish utilize dissolved oxygen in water through their gills rather than breaking down water molecules. This energy-releasing process is essential for life, ensuring that cells have the fuel required to function, grow, and repair themselves continuously.
summary: While breathing is inhaling and exhaling air to get oxygen, respiration is when your body uses oxygen to make energy and releases carbon dioxide. In plants, the tiny pores called stomata help plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide.
